**1 — Scene:** Roasted chicken with skin, a browned lobster tail, and a few thick-cut fries.

**2 — Vessel:** A dinner plate, approximately **26 cm** across. Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ **531 cm²**.

**3 — Items:** Chicken meat and skin, lobster meat, and fries. The meat has a glossy cooked surface; any cooking fat is included in the energy estimates rather than counted as a separate sauce.

**4 — Area:** Estimated edible footprints: chicken **15%**, lobster meat **9%**, fries **6%**—total **30%** of the plate. Exposed shell and bone occupy roughly another **7%**, giving about **37% total visible coverage**. Shell and bone are excluded from edible weight.

**5–7 — Volume, weight, and energy:** Heights below are average heights of the edible portions, not their tallest points.

| Item | Area | Average height | Gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated grams | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Chicken meat and skin | 80 cm² | 2.3 cm | 184 ml | 0.95 g/ml | 175 g | 230 | 403 kcal |
| Browned lobster meat | 48 cm² | 2.0 cm | 96 ml | 0.95 g/ml | 91 g | 140 | 127 kcal |
| Thick-cut fries | 32 cm² | 1.5 cm | 48 ml | 0.65 g/ml | 31 g | 310 | 96 kcal |

**8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **297 g edible food and 626 kcal** is plausible for two substantial protein portions and only a few fries on a mostly uncovered dinner plate. The main uncertainty is the amount of edible chicken versus bone and the cooking fat used.
